stories.title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Interpretability Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias
stories.author: Xiuying Chen
bullet_points: The research moves beyond input-output level analysis of LLM-as-Judge bias to investigate biases within the judge's internal hidden state (representation-level account).
This mechanistic interpretability approach offers a complementary and operationally more useful perspective on understanding and mitigating LLM judging biases.
The study provides extensive empirical validation across seven judges, seven bias types, and nine benchmarks.

stories.title: Evidence-Backed Video Question Answering
stories.author: Juan Carlos Niebles
bullet_points: Addresses the 'black box' problem in current Video LLMs by requiring verifiable visual grounding for answers.
Proposes Evidence-Backed Video Question Answering (E-VQA) to improve explainability beyond simple text or sparse bounding boxes.
Focuses on capturing complex video dynamics, such as occlusions and non-rigid deformations, which current models struggle with.

stories.title: MM-ToolSandBox: A Unified Framework for Evaluating Visual Tool-Calling Agents
stories.author: Afshin Dehghan
bullet_points: Introduces MM-ToolSandBox, a new benchmark and evaluation framework for visually grounded tool-calling agents.
The framework supports complex, stateful tasks involving 500+ tools across 16 application domains.
It specifically tests agents' ability to handle multi-image, multi-turn interactions, including goal revisions and error corrections.

stories.title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Interpretability Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias
stories.author: Xiuying Chen
bullet_points: The paper introduces a mechanistic interpretability approach to analyze bias in LLM-as-Judge systems, moving beyond traditional input-output level analysis.
It posits that judging biases can be understood at the representation level within the LLM's hidden state, offering a complementary analytical view.
The research provides empirical evidence across multiple judges, bias types, and benchmarks, detailing specific findings regarding judging geometry.

stories.title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Interpretability Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias
stories.author: Xiuying Chen
bullet_points: The paper moves beyond input-output level analysis of LLM-as-Judge bias to propose a mechanistic interpretability account within the judge's hidden state.
It offers a complementary and operationally useful perspective to existing bias mitigation strategies, which are primarily prompt-level.
The research is highly empirical, testing across seven judges, seven bias types, and nine benchmarks.

stories.title: Metacognition in LLMs: Foundations, Progress, and Opportunities
stories.author: Arman Cohan
bullet_points: Metacognition is identified as a critical, foundational element for advanced AI capabilities like learning and decision-making.
The paper addresses the current gap in understanding how and when Large Language Models (LLMs) can develop effective metacognitive abilities.
It frames the research as exploring the foundations, current progress, and future opportunities for integrating metacognition into AI systems.

stories.title: Invariant Learning Dynamics of Transformers in Inductive Reasoning Tasks
stories.author: Thomas Hofmann
bullet_points: Presents a theoretical framework to explain how Transformer models develop inductive reasoning abilities.
Unifies several existing synthetic inductive tasks, such as in-context n-grams and multi-hop reasoning, into a generalized class.
The research theoretically proves that the training dynamics of attention models can be constrained within this generalized task class.

stories.title: Transformer-Guided Swarm Intelligence for Frugal Neural Architecture Search
stories.author: Romain Amigon
bullet_points: Proposes a novel, frugal Neural Architecture Search (NAS) framework.
Combines a Transformer controller (using RL) for global search with local micro-exploitation.
Aims to democratize model design by enabling NAS on consumer-grade hardware, reducing massive computational costs.

stories.title: Requential Coding: Pushing the Limits of Model Compression with Self-Generated Training Data
stories.author: Andrew Gordon Wilson
bullet_points: The paper proposes 'Prequential Coding' as a new method to achieve model compression.
It addresses a limitation of traditional parameter-based compression (like quantization) where code length scales with model size.
The core idea is that a model's ability to represent data as a short code indicates it has discovered underlying regularities for better generalization.

stories.title: Invariant Learning Dynamics of Transformers in Inductive Reasoning Tasks
stories.author: Thomas Hofmann
bullet_points: Presents a theoretical framework explaining how Transformer models develop inductive reasoning abilities.
Studies a generalized class of inductive tasks, unifying previously disparate synthetic tasks like in-context n-grams and multi-hop reasoning.
The research theoretically proves that the training dynamics of attention models can be confined to a specific regime.

stories.title: A Minimalist Retargeting-Guided Reinforcement Learning Recipe for Dexterous Manipulation
stories.author: Preston Culbertson
bullet_points: Introduces REGRIND, a new minimalist pipeline for dexterous manipulation.
Addresses the challenge of applying simple motion retargeting recipes to complex, contact-rich manipulation tasks.
Utilizes Reinforcement Learning (RL) guided by retargeting to learn delicate control of contact modes and forces.

stories.title: Input-Aware Dynamic Backdoor Attack Against Quantum Neural Networks
stories.author: Rui Ning
bullet_points: The research addresses security vulnerabilities in Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs), a promising area of quantum machine learning.
It introduces a novel 'Input-Aware Dynamic Backdoor Attack,' moving beyond traditional fixed-trigger backdoor methods.
The dynamic nature of the attack is designed to evade existing defenses that target repetitive patterns left by static triggers.

stories.title: Transformer-Guided Swarm Intelligence for Frugal Neural Architecture Search
stories.author: Romain Amigon
bullet_points: Proposes a new, frugal Neural Architecture Search (NAS) framework to reduce computational demands.
Combines a Transformer controller (trained via RL) for global search with local micro-exploitation.
Aims to democratize model design by enabling NAS on consumer-grade hardware instead of requiring massive GPU resources.

stories.title: An Exact Instrument for State Usage in Selective State-Space Models, and the Input-Driven Migration It Reveals
stories.author: Raktim Bhattacharya
bullet_points: Introduces an exact measurement tool for how Selective State-Space Models (like Mamba) utilize their internal modes.
Leverages the diagonal nature of the state matrix to allow for exact decomposition of channel outputs into per-mode contributions.
Provides a method to quantify the output error incurred by selectively dropping subsets of modes offline, useful for model pruning/analysis.

stories.title: Metacognition in LLMs: Foundations, Progress, and Opportunities
stories.author: Arman Cohan
bullet_points: The paper addresses metacognition, a key component of intelligence, in the context of Large Language Models (LLMs).
It highlights that while LLMs show progress in tasks, their capacity for effective metacognitive abilities remains unclear.
The research focuses on the foundations, current progress, and future opportunities for integrating metacognition into AI systems.

stories.title: AdvancedMathBench: A Benchmark Suite for Advanced Mathematical Proof Generation and Verification
stories.author: Kai Chen
bullet_points: Introduces AdvancedMathBench, a new benchmark suite designed to test LLMs on advanced mathematical proof generation and verification.
Addresses the current limitation where existing benchmarks inadequately assess the reasoning process of LLMs in complex math.
Aims to bridge the gap between LLM performance on basic math and their capabilities in advanced, rigorous mathematical domains.

stories.title: How Temperature Shapes Ideological Discourse in Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
stories.author: Anderson Avila
bullet_points: The research investigates how 'Temperature' settings influence ideological discourse within Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.
It highlights a gap in current LLM research: the impact of ideological bias present in retrieved source material on final model outputs.
The study aims to determine if RAG systems transmit, amplify, or suppress existing ideological positions from their knowledge base.

stories.title: MET: Theory-Grounded and Culture-Aware Multilingual Moral Reasoning
stories.author: Lu Wang
bullet_points: Existing multilingual moral reasoning benchmarks fail because they rely on direct translation instead of adapting to culture-specific items.
Current inference methods for moral reasoning are limited by static, English-centric scaffolds and lack grounding in established moral theories.
Training approaches for moral decision-making are often hindered by the high cost of obtaining necessary supervision data.

stories.title: STEP: Career-Path Recommendation via Temporal and Educational Trajectory Modeling
stories.author: Tijl De Bie
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of analyzing career paths at scale by leveraging resumes, which are inherently unstructured and heterogeneous.
It proposes using Large Language Models (LLMs) to model temporal and educational trajectories within career paths.
The application has significant implications for workforce planning, labor market policy, and advanced job recommendation systems.

stories.title: Apple's new SpeechAnalyzer API, benchmarked against Whisper and its predecessor

bullet_points: Apple has released a new SpeechAnalyzer API.
The new API is being benchmarked against OpenAI's Whisper model.

stories.title: Porting Gemma-4 (2B / 4B / 12B) to AWS Inferentia2
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details the practical challenges of deploying Google's Gemma-4 models on AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
It highlights specific technical roadblocks encountered, including issues with mixed attention heads and limitations in existing optimization frameworks (vLLM, optimum-neuron, NxD).
The analysis provides a field report on compiler constraints (neuronx-cc) when targeting specialized inference hardware.

stories.title: GPT-5.6 Sol's file deletion isn't a bug you patch. It's proof that filtering an agent's actions doesn't contain it. Here's why, and what actually does.
stories.author: rbuckley_
bullet_points: The article discusses a critical incident where an AI agent (GPT-5.6 Sol) deleted a developer's files.
The core argument is that filtering agent actions is insufficient to contain advanced AI capabilities.
The piece promises to explain what truly controls or limits an AI agent's behavior.
